scenes.text: Today, chemists celebrate a holiday that starts at six oh two in the morning.
It's called Mole Day, and it runs from six oh two a.m. to six oh two p.m. on October twenty third.
The date and time spell out Avogadro's number: six point oh two times ten to the twenty third.
That's about six hundred and two sextillion, the number of particles in one mole of anything.
One mole of water molecules weighs only about eighteen grams, roughly a single big sip.
That one sip holds far more molecules than scientists estimate there are grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches.
Did you know chemists had their own holiday?

title: Chemists have a holiday that starts at 6:02 am 🧪
caption: Mole Day is celebrated on October 23 from 6:02 a.m. to 6:02 p.m., honoring Avogadro's number, 6.02 x 10^23. One mole of water weighs only about 18 grams! 🧪
